soundness_flags.label: ass:variance-change
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited Squires et al. model requires positive diagonal context variances and a generic changed structural row, but does not impose t_k != v_k for every intervention; retag this as a justified novel design restriction or cite a source that states it.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: sampling_model / prop:observable-quotient
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Recovery of aligned factor matrices and source laws from raw samples is an explicit population input, not a result claimed here.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All graph-compatibility and covariance-frontier claims are conditional on the aligned population factorization datum modulo common permutation and scaling.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Definition 3.14 defines soft(G) by baseline inverse-path rank equalities; Theorem 3.15 identifies that class with their model compatibility; Problems 5.1--5.2 ask for a combinatorial description and whether covariance compatibility is strictly larger.

The source assumes positive diagonal Omega_k and a generic single changed B-row; it treats variance-only change as a possible soft intervention but does not require every intervened variance to differ from baseline. It derives rank-one/two precision differences and recovers the soft-intervention transitive closure.

Under its generalized faithfulness assumptions, Theorem 1 identifies the transitive closure and Theorem 2 identifies the CD-equivalence class; this is a different target and assumption regime from the proposed positive covariance fiber.

The implicitization method assumes a rational inverse/global rational identifiability and strictly positive relevant denominators, so it does not itself supply finite chart coverage for a noninjective branch union.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag the universal variance-change condition as novel and give an application-level reason that every perturbation changes node noise variance; alternatively weaken it and rederive the branch statements with the variance-only degeneracy handled explicitly.

Make the compiler OEQ more falsifiable by first specifying a nontrivial graph family on which the proposed terminal-cut/branch-gluing route achieves an explicit bit bound, then state the general compiler as its extension.
Add a compact worked terminal-certificate calculation for the four-node mismatch, showing the actual-row minor and the failed published rank substitution side by side.

recommended_next_step: Repair the variance-change provenance, then advance the fork eight-branch classification as the Stage-0 first deliverable while retaining the compiler as the flagship open kernel.
